Proposition
[connection and curvature of a biinvariant metric]

Source: petersen:page-0158, petersen:page-0159 ↗ prop:pet-ch4-biinvariant-criterion ↗ def:pet-ch4-adjoint-action 1. ch4:4.4.2On a Lie group $G$ with biinvariant metric $(\cdot ,\cdot )$ and $X,Y,Z,W\in \mathfrak g$, \[ abla _YX= frac 12[Y,X],\qquad R(X,Y)Z=- frac 14[[X,Y],Z],\qquad R(X,Y,Z,W)= frac 14 ig([X,Y],[W,Z] ig). \] In particular, sectional curvature is always $\ge 0$.
Proof

↗ prop:pet-ch4-biinvariant-curvature-formula \sketch By subsection 4.1, differentiating the orthogonal adjoint action shows that every $\operatorname {ad}_X$ is skew-adjoint. The Koszul formula therefore reduces to $2( abla _YX,Z)=([Y,X],Z)$, hence $ abla _YX= frac 12[Y,X]$. Substitution in the curvature definition and the Jacobi identity give $R(X,Y)Z=- frac 14[[X,Y],Z]$. Skew-adjointness then yields $R(X,Y,Z,W)= frac 14([X,Y],[W,Z])$; for an orthonormal pair, $\operatorname {sec}(X,Y)= frac 14|[X,Y]|^2\ge 0$.

□
